summary.short: Sets cybersecurity risk-management and incident-reporting duties for essential and important entities in Annex I and II sectors, and requires Member States to designate national authorities, CSIRTs and cybersecurity strategies. Repeals Directive 2016/1148.
summary.long: Directive (EU) 2022/2555 sets measures for a high common level of cybersecurity across the Union and repeals Directive (EU) 2016/1148. It applies to public and private entities of the types listed in Annexes I and II that are medium-sized enterprises or larger and operate within the Union, and, regardless of size, to listed categories including electronic communications and trust service providers, TLD registries, DNS providers and critical entities under Directive (EU) 2022/2557. Entities are classed as essential or important. Member States must adopt national cybersecurity strategies, designate competent authorities, single points of contact, cyber crisis management authorities and CSIRTs, and compile lists of essential and important entities. Essential and important entities must take cybersecurity risk-management measures, which management bodies approve and oversee, and notify changes to their registration details. The Directive also establishes a Cooperation Group, a CSIRTs network, EU-CyCLONe, peer reviews, coordinated vulnerability disclosure and a European vulnerability database. The text provided covers the provisions up to Article 22; the remaining provisions are in the second part of the document.

notes: Part 1 of 2: covers Recitals (1)-(144) and Articles 1-22 up to Article 22(2). Relations and entities are coded from this part only; Article 22(3) onward and the Annexes are in part 2. Target instrument IDs and LEI/ticker fields are empty strings because no registry IDs or verified identifiers appear in the text (schema requires strings; codebook uses null). Essential and important entities, DNS, TLD and other provider categories are defined classes, not named entities, and are not listed under entities. Definitional references to other acts (Directive 2015/1535, Directive 2005/29/EC, Regulation (EU) 2019/1150, Regulation (EU) No 1025/2012) are not coded as relations here. The amending provisions for Regulation 910/2014 and Directive 2018/1972 are not in part 1; only the title and recital 92 refer to them. No internal inconsistencies identified in this part. Relations and entities are populated, so their section_status entries are set to not_applicable only because the schema requires the fields. Part 2 of 2 (Articles 23-46 and Annexes I-III); relations and entities are drawn only from this part. Annex I and II cross-references are recorded for the scope-defining definitions; other footnoted acts in the annexes are not each recorded as separate rows. Articles 31(10) and 33(6) print a sentence fragment after a full stop ('Regulation (EU) 2022/2554. with this Directive.'), reproduced as in the source. target_instrument_id is left empty because no registry IDs were supplied for the targets. lei and ticker are empty strings (schema requires strings) and are unverified. In section_status, relations and entities are populated above; the status values are a schema formality.

‘incident’ means an event compromising the availability, authenticity, integrity or confidentiality of stored, transmitted or processed data
‘large-scale cybersecurity incident’ means an incident which causes a level of disruption that exceeds a Member State’s capacity to respond to it
‘significant cyber threat’ means a cyber threat which, based on its technical characteristics, can be assumed to have the potential to have a severe impact
‘vulnerability’ means a weakness, susceptibility or flaw of ICT products or ICT services that can be exploited by a cyber threat
‘internet exchange point’ means a network facility which enables the interconnection of more than two independent networks

evidence.quote: ‘entity providing domain name registration services’ means a registrar or an agent acting on behalf of registrars
‘digital service’ means a service as defined in Article 1(1), point (b), of Directive (EU) 2015/1535
‘trust service provider’ means a trust service provider as defined in Article 3, point (19), of Regulation (EU) No 910/2014
‘qualified trust service provider’ means a qualified trust service provider as defined in Article 3, point (20), of Regulation (EU) No 910/2014
‘online marketplace’ means an online marketplace as defined in Article 2, point (n), of Directive 2005/29/EC
‘online search engine’ means an online search engine as defined in Article 2, point (5), of Regulation (EU) 2019/1150
‘cloud computing service’ means a digital service that enables on-demand administration and broad remote access to a scalable and elastic pool of shareable computing resources
‘data centre service’ means a service that encompasses structures, or groups of structures, dedicated to the centralised accommodation
‘content delivery network’ means a network of geographically distributed servers
‘social networking services platform’ means a platform that enables end-users to connect, share, discover and communicate with each other
‘representative’ means a natural or legal person established in the Union explicitly designated to act on behalf of
‘public administration entity’ means an entity recognised as such in a Member State in accordance with national law, not including the judiciary, parliaments or central banks
‘public electronic communications network’ means a public electronic communications network as defined in Article 2, point (8), of Directive (EU) 2018/1972
‘electronic communications service’ means an electronic communications service as defined in Article 2, point (4), of Directive (EU) 2018/1972
‘entity’ means a natural or legal person created and recognised as such under the national law
‘managed service provider’ means an entity that provides services related to the installation, management, operation or maintenance of ICT products
‘managed security service provider’ means a managed service provider that carries out or provides assistance for activities relating to cybersecurity risk management
‘research organisation’ means an entity which has as its primary goal to conduct applied research or experimental development

obligations.summary: Entities, competent authorities, single points of contact and CSIRTs process personal data only to the extent necessary for the Directive and in accordance with Regulation (EU) 2016/679.

evidence.quote: Entities, the competent authorities, the single points of contact and the CSIRTs shall process personal data to the extent necessary for the purposes of this Directive

obligations.summary: Confidential information is exchanged with the Commission and other authorities only where necessary for the application of the Directive, limited to what is relevant and proportionate, and its confidentiality is preserved.

evidence.quote: shall be exchanged with the Commission and other relevant authorities in accordance with this Directive only where that exchange is necessary for the application of this Directive

obligations.summary: Member States must adopt national cybersecurity strategies and designate or establish competent authorities, cyber crisis management authorities, single points of contact and CSIRTs (obligations stated in the scope of the Directive).

evidence.quote: obligations that require Member States to adopt national cybersecurity strategies

obligations.summary: Member States establish a list of essential and important entities and entities providing domain name registration services, and review and update it at least every two years thereafter.

evidence.quote: By 17 April 2025, Member States shall establish a list of essential and important entities

obligations.summary: Entities listed under Art. 3(3) submit to the competent authorities their name, address and up-to-date contact details, sector and subsector, and Member States where they provide services, and notify changes within two weeks of the change.

evidence.quote: Member States shall require the entities referred to in that paragraph to submit at least the following information to the competent authorities

obligations.summary: Competent authorities notify the Commission and the Cooperation Group of the number of essential and important entities per sector and subsector, and notify the Commission of further information on entities identified under Art. 2(2)(b) to (e).

evidence.quote: By 17 April 2025 and every two years thereafter, the competent authorities shall notify:

obligations.summary: The Commission provides guidelines clarifying the application of the sector-specific Union legal act provisions in Art. 4(1) and (2).

evidence.quote: The Commission shall, by 17 July 2023, provide guidelines clarifying the application of paragraphs 1 and 2.

obligations.summary: Each Member State adopts a national cybersecurity strategy with strategic objectives, resources, policy and regulatory measures, including the listed elements (governance, risk assessment, preparedness, policies on supply chain, procurement, vulnerabilities, education, active cyber protection); strategy is assessed on a regular basis and at least every five years.

evidence.quote: Each Member State shall adopt a national cybersecurity strategy that provides for the strategic objectives

obligations.summary: Member States notify their national cybersecurity strategies to the Commission within three months of their adoption, and may exclude national security information.

evidence.quote: Member States shall notify their national cybersecurity strategies to the Commission within three months of their adoption.

obligations.summary: Member States designate or establish one or more competent authorities for cybersecurity and supervisory tasks, and a single point of contact; they ensure adequate resources for these authorities and the single point of contact.

evidence.quote: Each Member State shall designate or establish one or more competent authorities responsible for cybersecurity

obligations.summary: Each Member State notifies the Commission without undue delay of the identity of the competent authority and single point of contact, their tasks and any changes, and makes the identity of its competent authority public.

evidence.quote: Each Member State shall notify the Commission without undue delay of the identity of the competent authority

obligations.summary: Each Member State designates or establishes one or more cyber crisis management authorities, ensures their adequate resources, identifies crisis capabilities, and adopts a national large-scale cybersecurity incident and crisis response plan with the elements listed.

evidence.quote: Each Member State shall designate or establish one or more competent authorities responsible for the management of large-scale cybersecurity incidents and crises

obligations.summary: Member States notify the Commission of the identity of the cyber crisis management authority within three months of its designation, and submit response plan information to the Commission and EU-CyCLONe within three months of adoption of the plans.

evidence.quote: Within three months of the designation or establishment of the cyber crisis management authority referred to in paragraph 1, each Member State shall notify the Commission

obligations.summary: Member States designate or establish one or more CSIRTs covering the sectors in Annexes I and II, ensure they have adequate resources and a secure communication and information infrastructure, and ensure their cooperation in the CSIRTs network and with entities and third-country CSIRTs.

evidence.quote: Each Member State shall designate or establish one or more CSIRTs.

obligations.summary: Each Member State notifies the Commission without undue delay of the identity of its CSIRTs and of the CSIRT designated as coordinator, and of their tasks and any changes.

evidence.quote: Each Member State shall notify the Commission without undue delay of the identity of the CSIRT referred to in paragraph 1

obligations.summary: CSIRTs comply with listed requirements (communication channels, secure sites, request routing, confidentiality, staffing, redundant systems) and jointly have the technical capabilities for the tasks listed in Art. 11(3), including monitoring, early warnings, incident response, forensic analysis and proactive scanning on request.

evidence.quote: The CSIRTs shall comply with the following requirements:

obligations.summary: Each Member State designates one of its CSIRTs as coordinator for coordinated vulnerability disclosure, which acts as trusted intermediary and enables anonymous vulnerability reporting, with follow-up and anonymity ensured.

evidence.quote: Each Member State shall designate one of its CSIRTs as a coordinator for the purposes of coordinated vulnerability disclosure.

obligations.summary: ENISA develops and maintains, after consulting the Cooperation Group, a European vulnerability database with the listed content and security measures.

evidence.quote: ENISA shall develop and maintain, after consulting the Cooperation Group, a European vulnerability database.

obligations.summary: Competent authorities, single points of contact and CSIRTs of the same Member State cooperate; CSIRTs or competent authorities receive significant incident notifications and incident, cyber threat and near-miss notifications, and inform the single points of contact; and cooperation with listed national authorities is ensured.

evidence.quote: Member States shall ensure that their CSIRTs or, where applicable, their competent authorities, receive notifications of significant incidents

obligations.summary: Member States simplify reporting through technical means for the notifications referred to in Art. 23 and Art. 30.

evidence.quote: Member States shall simplify the reporting through technical means for notifications referred to in Articles 23 and 30.

obligations.summary: The Cooperation Group, composed of Member State, Commission and ENISA representatives, carries out the listed tasks (guidance on transposition, information exchange, risk assessments of critical supply chains, mutual assistance discussion, peer review methodology, reports, state-of-play assessments); Member States ensure effective cooperation of their representatives.

evidence.quote: The Cooperation Group shall have the following tasks:

evidence.quote: By 1 February 2024 and every two years thereafter, the Cooperation Group shall establish a work programme

obligations.summary: The Cooperation Group meets regularly and at least once a year with the Critical Entities Resilience Group established under Directive (EU) 2022/2557.

evidence.quote: The Cooperation Group shall meet on a regular basis and in any event at least once a year with the Critical Entities Resilience Group

obligations.summary: The CSIRTs network carries out the listed tasks (information exchange, coordinated response, mutual assistance support, cooperation with SOCs, guidelines), and adopts its rules of procedure and procedural arrangements with EU-CyCLONe.

evidence.quote: The CSIRTs network shall have the following tasks:

obligations.summary: The CSIRTs network assesses progress on operational cooperation and adopts a report, with conclusions and recommendations based on peer reviews, submitted to the Cooperation Group.

evidence.quote: By 17 January 2025, and every two years thereafter, the CSIRTs network shall, for the purpose of the review

obligations.summary: EU-CyCLONe carries out the listed tasks (preparedness, shared situational awareness, impact assessment, coordination of crisis management, discussion of response plans), adopts its rules of procedure, and reports regularly to the Cooperation Group.

evidence.quote: EU-CyCLONe shall have the following tasks:

obligations.summary: EU-CyCLONe submits to the European Parliament and the Council a report assessing its work every 18 months.

evidence.quote: By 17 July 2024 and every 18 months thereafter, EU-CyCLONe shall submit to the European Parliament and to the Council a report

evidence.quote: Such agreements shall comply with Union data protection law.

evidence.quote: ENISA shall adopt, in cooperation with the Commission and the Cooperation Group, a biennial report on the state of cybersecurity in the Union

obligations.summary: The Cooperation Group, with the Commission and ENISA, establishes the methodology and organisational aspects of peer reviews on 17 January 2025.

evidence.quote: The Cooperation Group shall, on 17 January 2025, establish, with the assistance of the Commission and ENISA

obligations.summary: Member States ensure that management bodies of essential and important entities approve the cybersecurity risk-management measures taken under Art. 21 and oversee their implementation.

evidence.quote: Member States shall ensure that the management bodies of essential and important entities approve the cybersecurity risk-management measures

evidence.quote: Member States shall ensure that essential and important entities take appropriate and proportionate technical, operational and organisational measures

evidence.quote: By 17 October 2024, the Commission shall adopt implementing acts laying down the technical and the methodological requirements of the measures referred to in paragraph 2
